projects.description:
In summer 2019, WFP conducted formative research across Iraq to gain an in-depth understanding of people’s lives, attitudes, beliefs, habits, and practices around nutrition-related behaviours. Based on the research findings, in early 2020 workshops were held with ministry representatives, key stakeholders, national NGOs, UN agencies, and practitioners working in Iraq to prioritise the behaviours which are currently contributing to the high rate of obesity, overweight and micronutrient deficiency. 
 For each of the prioritised behaviours, WFP will work with partners to develop effective social behaviour change interventions and communication activities. To achieve sustainable behaviour change, WFP is drawing on advances within the behavioural science field to develop a series of interventions to support positive behaviour change, create new habit cues, and encourage social commitment.

projects.description:
Progress towards the achievement of the Result:
The security environment in Iraq remained fragile and protection of civilians continued to be a concern particularly in the context of security incidents resulting involving armed groups or pro-government militias. HRO monitored and documented security related incidents, harm to civilians and protection concerns From 1 January to 10 December 2020, HRO documented 458 security related incidents that resulted in 514 civilian casualties [198 deaths (including 15 women, 17 children, and 316 injuries (including 22 women, 46 children)], representing a 43 per cent decrease compared to the same period in 2019. UNAMI attributed 72 per cent civilian casualties to ISIL remnants in Iraq, 22 per cent to unknown armed groups, 5 per cent to Turkish forces, five per cent to pro-Government forces and the remaining one per cent to other armed actors, including pro-Government militias. Of the total, 36 per cent civilian casualties were caused by Improvised Explosive Devices (IEDs), 36 per cent by small arms fire, 10 per cent by the use of indirect fire (mortars), 5 per cent by air strikes and the remaining 13 per cent in explosive remnants of war or unexploded ordnance (UXOs), hand grenades and summary executions. Turkish military air strikes targeting the positions of PKK elements in the northern Iraq remained a concern as these air strikes also resulted in civilian casualties and/or caused damage to civilian property.
The Country Task Force on Monitoring and Reporting (CTFMR) documented 29 grave violations against children, affecting a total 20 children 17 girls and 3 boys (8 use of military schools in Kirkuk governorate and Salah al Din governorates, 11 abductions- late verification-, 7 cases of sexual violence (all girls), 1 case of recruitment and use of a boy, 1 case of attack on hospital and 1 case of denial of humanitarian access. On 2 May 2020, during a military operation against ISIL in the district of Yathrib, Salah al Dine Governorate, a boy used in the Popular Mobilization Forces was killed by an ISIL sniper and his body transferred to a local hospital.
HRO, jointly with UNICEF and Office of the SRSG Children and Armed Conflict, engaged with the Government of Iraq to finalize the National Action Plan on the recruitment and use of children and support their rehabilitation and reintegration. The support and technical assistance by UNAMI aligned the draft action plan with international standards. HRO , jointly with UNICEF and Justice Rapid Response, an international non-governmental organization, implemented a training programme for members of the CTFMR aimed at strengthening capacity of members of the Task Force for documentation of the child rights violations and to identify and address challenges faced in promoting protection for children. The workshop also launched a peer network as a continued exchange platform to strengthen the child protection framework in Iraq. HRO continue monitoring and reporting on the protection of civilians, including on the six gave child rights violations, provision of technical advice and support to the Government of Iraq to promote measures for the protection of civilians and the implementation of the Action Plan for the implementation of on the recruitment and use of children.

UNAMI and UNICEF Co-Chair the CTFMR in Iraq.
